newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac pledges to meet EMU deadlines.
newsitem.headline: Chirac pledges to meet EMU deadlines.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac said on Wednesday that France will meet all deadlines in the race to create a single European currency, government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said on Wednesday.
Chirac also said France and Germany would do everything that has to be done to respect the calendar for European Economic and Monetary Union, Lamassoure added.

"The president said that deadlines will be met and that despite the data released by certain economic institutes, the French government and the German government will both do everything necessary to respect the calendar and the conditions of the treaty on monetary union," Lamassoure told reporters after a cabinet meeting.

On Tuesday six leading German research institutes said Germany would fail to meet in 1997 the Maastricht-treaty criteria for the single currency because its public sector deficit was likely to be 3.5 percent of gross domestic product.
